extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of literature, poets and critics interested in classical Greek aesthetics
extracted.subtask_short: writing poetry in classical Greek mode
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for producing or evaluating poetry and art in the spirit of classical Greek literature — emphasising restraint, reasoned imagination, typified character, mythic/historical perspective, and unity that expresses the universal rather than accidental detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temperate restraint and rational control
rubrics_metrics.description: The Greek imagination is 'under the strict control of reason... limited by a sense of measure and a faculty of self-restraint.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for a reserve of power and 'temperate strength' — employ imaginative resources without effort or ostentation. The poet/artist should avoid dazzling for its own sake and be 'bent on seeing truly, on seeing harmoniously, and on expressing what he sees.' Anti-pattern: extravagant, uncontrolled ornament or showy virtuosity that distracts from truthful perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid grotesque hybrid symbolism
rubrics_metrics.description: Greek gods and artistic creations are not 'a thing half in the world, half out of it, no hybrid compound of symbolic attributes.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer intelligible, harmonious representations over strange symbolic hybrids (e.g., animal-headed deities). If symbolism is used it should be noble and subordinated to clarity. Anti-pattern: employing grotesque or irrational symbol mixes that confuse rather than illuminate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate the non-essential (focus on the essential)
rubrics_metrics.description: In assigning functions and attributes the Greeks 'eliminate' all that is non-essential; 'attributes which a god already has in common with other gods fall out.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trim redundant or non-distinctive traits; concentrate on defining, distinguishing attributes that serve the work's unity. This produces clear, type-like figures rather than cluttered, overlapping roles. Scoring note: works that pare to essentials score higher for clarity and typification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Underlying lawfulness even in fancy and comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Though comedy may 'revel in its own absurdities', 'even comedy has its lucid intervals... in its wildest freaks there is some underlying reason, some intelligible drift and purpose.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fantastic or absurd elements must still submit to an intelligible purpose or drift. Transitions between jest and earnest should feel purposeful, not arbitrary. Anti-pattern: pure, purposeless chaos with no detectable method or effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspiration subordinated to reason
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetic genius may be 'a form of madness' or 'inspired', but Greek poets 'never released themselves from the sovereignty of reason.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow ecstatic or inspired moments, but ensure the poet retains 'dominion over' the subject — the work must remain coherent and governed by judgement. Anti-pattern: works that excuse incoherence as mere inspiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim at the universal rather than the merely individual
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry 'represents the permanent possibilities of human nature, the essentials rather than the accidents' — it aims at the universal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose scenes, characters, and actions that reveal general truths or 'permanent possibilities' rather than idiosyncratic detail. The poetic sequence should show internal probability or necessity. Scoring: higher marks for works that articulate universals through concrete imaginative form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal probability and logical sequence over empirical detail
rubrics_metrics.description: The sequence of poetry is 'not the empirical sequence of fact but the logical or conceivable sequence of ideas; it eliminates chance and discovers unity and significance.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise causally or psychologically coherent progressions that express meaning and necessity within the piece rather than merely recounting events exactly as they happened. Anti-pattern: privileging factual minutiae at the expense of thematic coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typification in characterization (reduction to elemental types)
rubrics_metrics.description: Greek heroines are 'broadly and unmistakably human' and can be 'reduced to certain elemental types of womanhood' — maiden, wife, mother, daughter, sister — which provide a stable groundwork for character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use archetypal/typical relations to give characters universal resonance. Individual detail is permitted only insofar as it contributes to the 'total impression' and remains subject to the controlling unity of the work. Anti-pattern: excessive eccentric individuality that prevents recognition of broader human types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admit variety of detail only when contributory to total impression
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'utmost variety of detail is admitted, if only it contributes to the total impression and is subject to a controlling unity of design.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow nuanced particulars, but evaluate details by whether they enhance the central design and unity. Remove or downplay details that distract. Scoring note: coherence of details with the whole is a key criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry as sensuous, concrete philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry is 'akin to philosophy in so far as it aims at expressing the universal; but... it employs the medium of sensuous and imaginative form. In this sense poetry is a concrete philosophy, "a criticism of life".'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use imagery, narrative, and embodied form to convey interpretive or philosophical views of life rather than abstract exposition. Judge works on how well imaginative form embodies a consistent wisdom or interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use myth and historic perspective to elevate the present
rubrics_metrics.description: Myth was for the Greeks 'the unwritten literature of an early people' and served to 'project' the present into the past so the ode or poem 'rises by clear ascents from the individual to the universal.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Situate individual events in larger mythic or historical contexts to provide perspective and magnify significance (Pindaric model). Anti-pattern: treating recent or painful events without temporal distance that prevents imaginative elevation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideal as fulfilment of the real
rubrics_metrics.description: The Greek ideal 'was not the opposite of the real, but rather its fulfilment and perfection.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conceive ideals as intensified, perfected expressions of observed reality rather than abstract opposites; aesthetic choices should feel organically rooted in experience. Anti-pattern: creating an ideal that feels detached or contrived relative to observed reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanity and corrective judgement in genius
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'perfect sanity of the Greek genius' — the true poet 'dreams being awake' and 'has dominion over' his subject; 'insanity is a kind of disordered individualism.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether imaginative leaps are checked by judgement and whether the poet aligns individual vision with universal human reason. Penalise egoistic, uncorrected flights that disregard shared human norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: History and myth as fused, authentic material
rubrics_metrics.description: Greek myth often functioned as 'authentic history' — 'truth and fiction were here fused together, and the collective whole was heroic history.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat legendary or mythic material as a legitimate way to encode social memory and moral/human truths; evaluate how effectively the work fuses imaginative shaping with credible cultural or historical feeling. Anti-pattern: treating myth merely as ornament without integrating meaning.
